title: A 3:30 AM finish is not just a scheduling problem. It’s a sleep problem.
hook: A 3:30 AM finish is not just a scheduling problem. It’s a sleep problem.
caption:
A 3:30 AM finish is not just a scheduling problem. It’s a sleep problem.

@carlitosalcarazz 
Carlos has called out what happens when elite athletes finish competing in the early hours.
A 3:30 finish can mean leaving the venue at 4:30, getting back to the hotel, eating, decompressing — and finally getting into bed at 6:30 or 7 AM.

And then we expect the athlete to recover and perform again.

Sleep isn’t what happens after sport. Sleep is part of sport.

Maybe it’s time we stopped looking at competition schedules and athlete recovery as two separate conversations.

The match ends at 3:30 AM.
